turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: The maid, timid and respectful, asked O-lan if she was feeling a little better now, and if there was anything she could do for her.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that she must rest now and worry about the future later, that he would take care of their son and see to his marriage and prosperity, but O-lan must save her strength for herself.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan looked at Wang Lung and told him that she knew he would not be able to do what she asked, that he was still grieving for her, and that she must see this one thing through before she died.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung insisted that O-lan must not exhaust herself with worries about their son's future, that he would provide for him and ensure his marriage to a good woman, but she must think of her own recovery and well-being.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that he would not have her exhaust herself with thoughts of their son's future, for it was only right that their eldest son should take care of his own family, and that he would make sure the young man was provided for, but O-lan must focus on her own recovery.

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: The maid asked Wang Lung if he had given any thought to the marriage arrangements for their son, and if he thought it wise to bring a matchmaker to the house soon.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung told the maid that he had given much thought to their son's marriage and that he had already begun to consider suitable matches, but now was not the time to discuss such things with O-lan so weak and ill.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan turned to the maid and asked if she had heard of any suitable matches for their eldest son, her voice weak but insistent.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that she must not think of these things, that she must rest and recover, and that he would handle the marriage arrangements for their son, as he always had.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son told his mother, O-lan, that he did not want her to worry about his marriage, that he was young and it was not yet time for him to think about such things, but that he would make sure to take good care of himself and bring honor to their family.

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: The maid asked O-lan if she would like her to go out to the village and ask about any suitable matches for their son, hoping to find someone who could help with the arrangements.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son told his mother that he would go to the village with the maid, so that she wouldn't have to exert herself, and they could speak to the matchmaker together.

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: The maid told Wang Lung that she would be happy to go to the village, but she was worried about her mother-in-law's health and whether it would be too much for her to be out and about.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan told the eldest son and the maid that she was glad they would go to the village, but that she still had many things to do before she could rest, and she asked them to be sure to speak to the matchmaker about a woman who had been a good match for their son's aunt.

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: The maid asked Wang Lung if he would please make sure that O-lan was not overexerting herself, and that the maid could help in any way she could.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that she was counting on him to see to the marriage arrangements and that the matchmaker should be told to hurry, for time was running out.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son asked his father if he had made any progress in speaking to the matchmaker about his own marriage, and if the matchmaker had any suitable candidates in mind.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that he would see to it, but he needed her to rest and not worry about the matchmaker for now, that he would handle everything and she should concentrate on getting better.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan looked at Wang Lung with a determined expression and asked if he had spoken to the matchmaker yet, and if the woman he had chosen for their son was suitable, as she had been troubled by the thought of the match all day.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son told his father that he was anxious to please Mother and start his new life, and he trusted Father to choose a suitable bride for him.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that there was another thing she had to attend to before she could die.

opening.speaker: Wang Lung
opening.text: Wang Lung insisted that O-lan should not speak of dying and that it would please him if she did not.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan replied that she had to die, for she felt it in her vitals waiting, but she would not die before her eldest son came home and before he wedded this good maid who was her daughter-in-law, and well she served O-lan, holding the hot water basin steadily and knowing when to bathe O-lan's face when she sweated in pain. Now O-lan wanted her son to come home, because she had to die, and she wanted him to wed this maid first, so that she might die easily, knowing that her grandson was stirred into life and a great-grandson for the old one.

opening.speaker: Wang Lung
opening.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that she looked twice as well as they had said and years away from death.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan declared that she would see Wang Lung wedded and then she must die.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan instructed Wang Lung to sit there and drink the wine and eat the rice of his marriage, for she would see it all and this would be his bed of marriage since she was soon to be finished with it and carried away.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan asked if everyone had wine, if the sweet rice dish in the middle of the feast was very hot, if they had put full measure of lard and sugar into it, and if the eight fruits were present.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that she was now content and that this thing in her may do as it would. She instructed her son to look to his father and his grandfather, and her daughter to look to her husband and his father and his grandfather and the poor fool in the court, there she was. And she told Wang Lung that he had no duty to any other.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan said that, even if she was ugly, she had borne a son; although she was but a slave, there was a son in her house.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan insisted that no one else could feed Wang Lung's son and care for him as she did. She told Wang Lung that beauty would not bear a man sons.
